criteria.criterion: Injected Python/native-like hang/crash/OOM/output flood gets classified and bounded
criteria.detail: Real spawned children (never mocks of the supervisor): hang -> timeout/wall with SIGTERM->grace->SIGKILL process-group kill; SIGTERM-ignoring child escalates to SIGKILL; real SIGSEGV -> failed/crash; memory growth -> failed/memory_limit via live RSS probe (libproc macOS, /proc Linux) plus RLIMIT_AS in-child where accepted; stdout/stderr floods -> failed/output_limit with bounded head+tail samples only; nonzero exit -> failed/exit; spawn failure -> failed/spawn_error; leaked same-group descendants reaped after leader exit. Post-review fix: a stream over cap whose excess was only drained in _drain_until_eof AFTER reap now also classifies failed/output_limit (test_post_reap_output_overflow_is_classified reproduces the sibling-blocked drain at jobs=2; verified red pre-fix). Committed F20 worker-fault-* fixture scenarios exercised through tests/fixtures/fault_double.py. All bounds enforced by the parent poll loop, never SIGALRM.

Committed report bytes are the child's produced bytes verbatim: tmp-sibling write -> fsync -> os.replace -> directory fsync (atomic_write_bytes); test_identical_runs_produce_byte_identical_reports asserts byte-identical reports across runs; resume verifies sha256 + config_digest and marks the job skipped without rewriting. A failed/killed sibling never touches a completed job's committed report.

limits.retries defaults to native.max_retries = 1; only transient kinds (exit, crash, wall, spawn_error) retry, each with a fresh worker and fresh scratch, only while run_wall_seconds leaves room. test_retry_is_bounded_to_one asserts attempts stop at 2; test_run_deadline_preempts_retry asserts no retry past the deadline. output_limit, memory_limit, missing_output, report_invalid and cancelled are never retried.
Exit 0 without a declared output completes with attempts == 1, never retried. Exit 0 with a declared-but-absent output is failed/missing_output - deterministic defect, also never retried.

criteria.criterion: Ctrl-C terminates descendants and leaves valid partial artifact.
criteria.detail: SIGINT/SIGTERM to the supervisor (or request_cancel) forwards to a cancel: every live process group is SIGTERM->SIGKILL terminated including leaked descendants, queued jobs get terminal cancelled records (I05), and index.json + journal.jsonl are still written so the partial artifact stays valid (driver-level SIGINT test; in-process SIGINT test).

criteria.criterion: One task failure does not poison the whole corpus (I17 containment)
criteria.detail: A crashing/hanging job terminates failed/timeout while earlier and later jobs still complete and commit reports; run status is 'partial', and index.json records a terminal record for every planned job.

criteria.criterion: jobs default 1; PDFium/reader calls stay out of concurrent threads
criteria.detail: Limits.jobs defaults to native.default_jobs = 1; jobs > 1 requires an explicit CPU/RAM-aware ParallelAdmission and is refused otherwise. The supervisor uses zero threads and zero engine calls - all reader calls execute inside child processes only, so PDFium is never invoked from concurrent threads (s26).

environment.note: RLIMIT_AS is rejected by macOS; on this host the memory bound is the live libproc RSS probe + post-exit wait4 ru_maxrss. Linux adds in-child RLIMIT_AS and /proc VmRSS probing. rlimit_support is recorded per run in index.json.

limitations: Verified on macOS arm64 only in this worktree; the Linux rlimit path (RLIMIT_AS, /proc RSS) is implemented and probed but awaits the Homebase/Linux verification round.

Memory bound is layered and degraded where the platform refuses rlimits (macOS RLIMIT_AS): the RSS probe polls at 100 ms so a child could briefly exceed the bound before the kill lands; a container remains the hardened route per THREAT_MODEL.
RLIMIT_CPU is only a backstop (wall deadline +60 s); the authoritative deadline is the parent's poll loop.
Unreapable D-state children are recorded as 'abandoned' (journal child_unreaped, job classified) rather than hanging the run forever.

A supervisor killed hard (SIGKILL/power loss) cannot reap: committed reports and the journal stay intact but index.json is absent, so resume is honestly refused and a fresh run refuses the non-empty dir - recovery is a new run directory, never a clobber or silent reuse (README 'Honest limits').
Limits.retries is caller-configurable above the native.max_retries default; the one-retry bound is enforced relative to the configured value (sanctioned config surface, noted by review).
The single native/tests/ocr failure on this host is a T27-owned macOS path-canonicalization issue outside T29 scope; preserved verbatim, not weakened.
Resume refuses a changed per-job config digest (new run directory required) - stricter than silently rerunning, per the byte-stability contract.
